runs.rationale_summary: Provider stall, not a misranking. The agent made 4 API calls in 21 s: the getCategoryStart body with the buggy line on screen (msg 7), the test source, failing_tests showing expected 30.0 but was 56.67 (msg 12), and the calculate* helpers. After that no model response came back; the harness killed it at 300 s with no exit status and no submission.

The agent correctly read the test values (112.5 vs 87.5) as a right-size, wrong-sign displacement. It then blamed drift (H3) because it 'computes dx and dy as point1 minus point2', the line that looks backwards, and treated shift's addition as correct. It read the 3-line ShapeUtilities.shift body (msg 30), submitted on the next turn, and put the chain in call order: drift, facade, ring, rim, nudge, then shift at rank 6.

Same pattern as run-002. The evidence chain says that 'for movement from the unexploded point to the exploded point' drift's point1 - point2 differences 'are sign-reversed', and it cites the drift, nudge and shift lines together. That assumes shift's additive displacement convention without checking it, so the vector's producer is blamed rather than its consumer. The gold body was read (msg 36) just before submitting, and shift ended up at rank 6, behind the whole chain.

The agent used the writer layout to get offset 156 vs 148, then called the facade parseTarHeader 'the direct and strongest fault candidate' because it is where the checksum byte is read. It ranked checksumBoundary (H4, named after the checksum) 2nd, saying it 'ultimately returns numericEnd unchanged', ahead of flagOffset. Yet flagOffset's 'afterChecksum = numericEnd' body was displayed in full (msg 32) right before submission. The unused CHKSUMLEN import in the gold file was never fetched.

The agent found and integrated everything it needed: the facade javadoc 'in bits', the sibling 'i * 16 + dstPos', the inverse longToIntArray, and jshell probes of both the facade and overlay showing 0F123456 instead of 0F12345600. Its evidence chain even says overlay 'contains the concrete arithmetic most directly explaining both assertions'. It still ranked intArrayToLong 1st as 'the directly tested production method [that] delegates all nontrivial work'.

Provider stall. The agent made 3 API calls in 18 s: it ran the test (no values found), read the facade javadoc and guard ('in bits'), the foldValues delegation, and the sibling and inverse idioms. Then no model response came back; it was killed at 300 s, still at hop 1, with no submission.

Provider stall after 5 API calls in 37 s. The agent read the facade javadoc, the sibling and inverse idioms and the sibling tests, followed foldValues to the Fraction.assemble call, and grepped the assemble signature (msgs 18-19). It never got the body on screen: no further model response came back and the harness killed it at 300 s.

Provider stall after 7 API calls in 43 s. The agent saw failing_tests (expected 305419776 but was 1311767949471645696) and decoded it to hex as 0x1234560000000000. It displayed the BitField.lane body with the ceiling-division fault line (msg 24) and was checking the Conversion siblings when no further model response arrived. It was killed at 300 s with no submission.

The run ended with exit_status RateLimitError (insufficient_quota, no credits remaining) after 5 API calls. By then the agent had seen expected 64729929216 but was 252851286, read the facade javadoc and siblings, and was at hop 1 (ArrayUtils.gather). It never reached LocaleUtils.lodge.

Provider stall after only 2 API calls in 6 s. The full safeNorm body, including the fault line 'norm = x1max * Math.sqrt(s1 + s2 / x1max)', was displayed at msg 6. No model response came back after that; it was killed at 300 s with no submission.

Provider stall after 4 API calls in 25 s. The safeNorm body was on screen (msg 6), and a jshell probe reproduced the failing value 4.898979485566356E19 for [2e19, 1e10] (msg 10). The agent was browsing other norm code when model responses stopped; it was killed at 300 s.

Provider stall after 12 API calls and 30 tool calls in 107 s. A jshell probe reproduced 4.898979485566356E19. The agent traversed survey, balance, residue and settle in order, and its last step displayed the FastMath.merge body with 'relative = plain / scale' (msg 43). No further model response came back; it was killed at 300 s before submitting.

The agent made 13 API calls in 56 s: it traversed the full chain, displayed the merge body (msg 28), and ran a jshell probe of safeNorm and merge. The next model call took about 358 s, so the agent's own wall clock fired (exit TimeExceeded) before it could submit. The time went to provider latency, not to investigation.

Only 1 API call. Its 3 tool results (grep for safeNorm, the defects4j test, a file count) were stamped 529 s after the model response, and the agent's clock fired (TimeExceeded) before a second step. It was a harness or environment stall, and investigation never started.

pattern: Of the 14 wrong runs in this half (even positions), 10 are infrastructure no-answers, not localization misses. Nine are timeouts and one is a provider_error. In 7 of the timeouts the agent worked normally for 6-107 s (2-12 API calls), then no model response came back until the harness killed it at 300 s. MATH-NORM-TREATMENT run-004 lost its time to one 358-s model call, and run-006 to a 529-s tool stall. LANG-CONV-CAMOUFLAGE-LOW run-002 ended with RateLimitError (insufficient_quota). In 6 of these 10 runs (CHART-AXIS, HA-LOW, both MATH-NORM-CONTROL, MATH-NORM-TREATMENT 001/004) the gold body had already been displayed. The 4 runs that actually answered wrong all ran the test, saw the failure values, read the gold method in full and pulled in the external evidence, so none is a search or retrieval failure. All 4 are ownership errors made after reading the gold. (a) CHART-PIE-TREATMENT-03 runs 002 and 004 rank the definer PlotUtilities.drift 1st, because its point1 - point2 line looks backwards and shift's additive convention is assumed correct; the gold sits at rank 6, behind the whole chain in call order. (b) CMP-LAYOUT-TREATMENT-02 run-004 and CONVERSION-DISPATCH-TREATMENT-01 run-003 rank the directly tested facade 1st ('direct and strongest' / 'directly tested production method'), putting the gold at 3 and 2. In DISPATCH run-003 the agent even wrote that overlay best explains both assertions.
